inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 30 June 2026: FY2025 RMB5,130m + H1 FY2026 RMB4,629m - H1 FY2025 RMB2,418m (H1 FY2026 IR cash-flow statement, 'Payment on repurchase of shares'). The count is held flat, so buybacks are value-neutral here; they are recorded to show the flat count is being funded in cash (159.3m shares cancelled in H1 FY2026 at HK$30.12-35.00).
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1727 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16T11:07Z). Cross-check via USD legs: USDHKD 7.8479 / USDCNY 6.6755 = 1.1756, a 0.25% tie that confirms direction and magnitude. No dual listing exists for a parity check; the Group's Shenzhen-listed subsidiary (002379.SZ) is not a proxy for the parent. All per-share values are computed in CNY and multiplied by fx_rate to HKD; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD, comparable to current_price.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30 June 2026 (FY2025 + H1 FY2026 - H1 FY2025), not FY2025, because the balance sheet anchors are at 30 June 2026 and already contain H1 FY2026's cash generation; compounding FY2026 from a December base would count H1 FY2026 FCF twice. TTM revenue 162,354 + 87,506 - 81,039 = 168,821. TTM attributable NI 27,485; TTM PBT 40,436; TTM D&A 7,192; TTM share of associates 1,886; TTM interest income 1,596.
inputs.share_count_basis: 9,819.4m issued at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 IR note 30 and cover page) plus 127.7m shares from the US$300m 2025 CBs on an if-converted basis (conversion price reset to HK$18.44 at 30 June 2026, in the money at the current price; US$300m x 7.8479 / 18.44). The RMB10.2bn 2026 CBs (conversion HK$43.90, zero coupon, due 2027) are far out of the money and are carried as debt at face, not as shares. Held FLAT: SBC is zero and buybacks are the mechanism keeping the count flat. The CSV's H1 FY2026 figure of 9,925m is the weighted-average basic count, not the period-end count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Debt at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 IR balance sheet, RMB m): bank borrowings 14,420 + 21,445 = 35,865; medium-term debentures and bonds 1,497 + 14,157 = 15,654; guaranteed notes 4,064; 2026 CBs at face 10,200 (liability component 9,435 accretes to 10,200 at the 2027 maturity); lease liabilities 95 + 995 = 1,090 (treatment A, leases as debt). Total 66,873. The 2025 CB liability (1,551) and both CB derivative components (867) are excluded because the 2025 CBs are treated as converted in the share count. Cash: cash and equivalents 46,144 + time deposits over three months 3,525 = 49,669. Restricted bank deposits (2,746) are excluded conservatively although they secure part of the borrowings deducted. Net debt 17,204.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. Risk-free 1.8% (10y China Government Bond), ERP 7.0% (4.5% mature + 2.5% China country risk), beta 1.3 for a commodity-price-taker -> cost of equity 10.9%. Pre-tax cost of debt 3.6% (bank loans ~3%, bonds 0-7.05%), 25% tax -> 2.7%. Market weights D/V 28% (debt RMB67bn vs market cap RMB164bn). WACC = 0.72 x 10.9 + 0.28 x 2.7 = 8.6%, rounded to 8.5%. Same rate in every scenario: cyclicality, alumina oversupply and Guinea risk are charged in the flows and the scenario weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities RMB1,090m included in total_debt; lease principal (RMB136m H1 FY2026) NOT deducted from the flows; right-of-use depreciation (RMB327m FY2025) stays inside D&A so it reduces EBIT for cash tax, and the capex path covers renewal. Right-of-use assets of RMB10.1bn are mostly prepaid PRC land-use rights, which carry no liability.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: non-controlling interests deducted at book value RMB10,410m (30 June 2026; up from 9,117m after the January 2026 restructuring that lifted the stake in Shandong Hongqiao Aluminum Industry Holding, 002379.SZ, to ~89%). Flows are left on a 100% consolidated basis. NCI took 6.3% of FY2025 profit and 9.9% of H1 FY2026 profit; book NCI is 7.3% of total equity, so the book deduction is in line with the profit share. Calibration: TTM clean NOPAT 30.2bn - after-tax finance costs 2.5bn + after-tax interest income 1.2bn + associates 1.9bn - NCI 2.2bn = 28.6bn vs reported attributable NI 27.5bn (4% gap, the 26.5% reported tax rate vs the 25% modelled).
inputs.mid_cycle_note: PEAK-EARNINGS MID-CYCLING APPLIED. Clean EBITDA margin (PBT + finance costs + D&A - share of associates - interest income, over revenue): FY2018 21.0%, FY2019 24.3%, FY2020 26.7%, FY2021 28.0%, FY2022 16.2%, FY2023 18.1%, FY2024 25.4%, FY2025 24.3%, TTM Jun-2026 28.1% (H1 FY2026 alone ~32%, a record, with aluminium ASP +18.7% YoY). Eight-year mean 23.0%. The base case starts at 26.5% in Y1 and fades to a 23.5% mid-cycle margin by Y3, held flat; it does not capitalise the current peak. Capex is normalised to 5.5% of revenue (RMB9-10bn, the FY2021-25 average of RMB8.8bn/yr) rather than the RMB3.7bn H1 FY2026 run-rate, tapering to 4.5% (just above D&A at 4.3%) once the Yunnan park and Indonesian alumina build-out complete.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied: (a) currency - CNY flows and CNY WACC, HKD quote with an explicit fx_rate; (b) leases as debt; (c) NCI deducted once in the bridge; (d) matching-asset rule - interest income (RMB1,596m TTM, including SOFR+3-5% interest on RMB9.3bn of loans to associates and the 4.33-5.78% CITIC Trust products) and share of associates' profit (RMB1,886m TTM) are OUTSIDE the EBITDA-based flows, so cash, time deposits, loans to associates, interests in associates, the trust products, FVTPL funds and FVOCI stakes are all in the bridge; (e) SBC-zero market, SBC rows kept explicit at 0%, house = street, band collapses; (f) risk charged once, in the flows and the weights. The business is a volume-capped commodity producer: 6.46Mt of compliant smelting capacity under China's ~45Mt cap means revenue growth is aluminium-price and mix driven, so the selected growth rate is a nominal 2.5%, not the 13.5% five-year revenue CAGR that was driven by the aluminium price rising from ~RMB14k/t to ~RMB20k/t+. Simandou: the US$1.78bn JV funding guarantee is not modelled as an outflow and no Simandou dividends are modelled as an inflow - the stake sits in the bridge at book inside interests in associates (RMB18.0bn); treated as symmetric optionality. Price context: the stock closed HK$20.06 on 30 June 2026 (CB valuer input) after buybacks at HK$30-35 in H1 FY2026 and HK$32.62 at December 2025; it has halved from the 52-week high while H1 FY2026 net profit rose 39%, so the market is pricing a cycle turn harsher than this model's bear case - see valuation_philosophy for the no-re-rate memo.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: volume-capped commodity producer; nominal aluminium-price and mix growth, not any historical CAGR
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2022->FY2025 (3y) and FY2020->FY2025 (5y). Owner FCF = reported FCF - interest income (SBC is zero): FY2020 11,890; FY2022 -1,928 (negative, so the 3-year owner-FCF CAGR is undefined); FY2025 26,904. The 36.6% 3-year EPS CAGR starts from the FY2022 trough (EPS 0.94) and the 7.2% revenue CAGR from a peak-revenue year, so neither is a trend; every historical rate here is a point in the aluminium cycle. Equity 5y 13.2% vs revenue 5y 13.5% vs EPS 5y 14.3% are within 30% of each other, so no divergence flag, but none of them is used as the forward rate: smelting volume cannot grow beyond the 6.46Mt compliant quota.

base.narrative: Aluminium stays tight through mid-2027 on the China cap (Y1 margin 26.5%), then the price normalises and alumina stays oversupplied: revenue dips 3% in Y2 and the margin settles at the 23.5% mid-cycle level from Y3. Volumes flat at the quota; nominal growth 2.5% thereafter. Capex normalised to RMB9-10bn then tapering toward D&A. Cash tax 25% (statutory; TTM cash rate 23.8%, book rate 26.5%). Working capital consumes 15% of each revenue increase (receivables + inventory RMB52.6bn vs payables RMB23.7bn). Terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF - the cyclical cap - which binds below Gordon at 8.5%/2.0%.

bull.narrative: The capacity cap holds and global ex-China supply growth disappoints, keeping aluminium near record levels; Indonesian alumina self-sufficiency and Yunnan hydropower structurally lift the mid-cycle margin to 26% (above the FY2020-21 and FY2024-25 peaks' average, below the H1 FY2026 32% print); fabrication/NEV mix adds nominal growth of 3%. Same WACC, cap and capex path as base - the bull axis is price and cost position, not multiple.

bear.narrative: The cycle turns the way the share price since Q2 2026 implies: a China demand/property slowdown plus faster ex-China (Indonesian) supply pushes aluminium down, revenue falls 10% in Y2, and the margin revisits the FY2022-23 trough (16-17%) for two years; alumina oversupply persists; policy (export-rebate, cap loosening) or Guinea instability stops the margin recovering past 18.5% - a permanently lower mid-cycle than the 23% history. Capex is cut to maintenance. Working capital releases cash in the downturn (negative capture on falling revenue).

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle normalisation: 26.5% EBITDA margin in the year to June 2027 fading to the 23.5% eight-year mean by Y3, flat volumes at the 6.46Mt quota, 2.5% nominal growth, capex normalised to RMB9-10bn, terminal value capped at 12x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Capacity cap plus Indonesia/Yunnan cost position hold the mid-cycle margin at 26% with 3% nominal growth; aluminium stays structurally tight through the decade.
scenario_narratives.bear: Two-year trough at 16-17% margin on a China demand downturn and ex-China supply, with the recovery capped at 18.5% by policy or Guinea risk; revenue falls 10% in Y2 and only recovers 2%/yr.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: this is a commodity price-taker sitting at a record H1 FY2026 margin, the alumina leg has already collapsed from 35% to 6% gross margin, Guinea (bauxite JV and Simandou) is a single-country political risk, and the stock halving from HK$41 to HK$19.64 while profits rose 39% says the market expects a cycle turn. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs aluminium to stay at record levels AND the cap to hold AND Indonesian alumina to earn its keep simultaneously. Base 50%. No live corporate action, so the three-scenario frame stands.

valuation_philosophy.summary: China Hongqiao is valued as a volume-capped, vertically integrated aluminium producer on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the record H1 FY2026 print: the base case fades the clean EBITDA margin from 28% (TTM) to the 23.5% eight-year mean, normalises capex to the RMB9-10bn five-year average, caps the terminal value at 12x FCF, and discounts in CNY at 8.5%. Non-operating assets (associates incl. Simandou at book, loans to associates, CITIC trust products, FVTPL funds with a 25% LP haircut, FVOCI) are added in the bridge because their income is outside the flows; NCI is deducted once at book. The per-share value is computed in CNY and converted to HKD at 1.1727. No-re-rate memo: the stock has historically traded at 4-8x P/E and 3-5x EV/EBITDA; at 5x EV/EBITDA on the RMB40bn mid-cycle EBITDA the equity is ~RMB21/share (~HK$25), which is the price of the no-re-rating view and still above the current quote - the market at 6x TTM P/E and ~3x EV/EBITDA is pricing a permanent FY2022-23-style trough, harsher than this model's bear case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Aluminium price: every 1pp of mid-cycle EBITDA margin is ~RMB1.7bn of EBITDA and roughly RMB1.3/share (HK$1.5) of value; the base 23.5% could be 2-3pp too high if the FY2022-23 trough was the new normal
Alumina oversupply persisting (segment gross margin 35% -> 6% in three periods) with Indonesian capacity still ramping industry-wide
Guinea political risk on the bauxite JV and Simandou, plus the US$1.78bn Simandou funding guarantee that is not modelled as an outflow
China capacity-cap policy loosening, or export-rebate and 'dual carbon' compliance costs compressing fabrication and smelting margins

Bridge quality: RMB45bn of non-operating assets (associates at book, PRC limited partnerships, CITIC Trust products) carry counterparty and valuation risk; a 50% haircut on all of them is ~RMB2.2/share (HK$2.6)
CNY/HKD rate: the valuation is in CNY; a 5% CNY depreciation is a 5% cut to the HKD value
Governance: Zhang family control, related-party loans to associates at SOFR+3-5%, and the discount HK-listed private Chinese industrials carry may never close

Re-rating dependence: the house value needs the market to pay ~12x owner FCF at exit against a 10-year history of 2-7x EV/EBITDA and 4-13x P/E; without any re-rating the value is ~HK$25 (see sanity_check_note)
